clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old male with a history of cryptorchidism presented with a 1-year history of left scrotal swelling, recently complicated by local hyperemia and pain. Physical examination revealed a large, hard, painful left testicular tumor with inflamed adjacent tissues. Initial blood work showed elevated inflammatory markers (WBC, ESR, fibrinogen, ALP). Ultrasonography indicated structural modifications characteristic of testicular malignancy. A left radical orchiectomy was performed without complications. The known final diagnosis is cribriform and pseudoglandular pattern seminoma, with T2N0 stage stadialization, although the specific histopathology report was not provided as observed evidence.
